newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls U.S. a bully for bombing Iraq.
newsitem.headline: China calls U.S. a bully for bombing Iraq.

text.p: China on Thursday branded the United States a bully for firing missiles at Iraq and called on both countries to halt military action in the Gulf.
Beijing's latest criticism of the two cruise missile attacks highlighted China's increasing anger over the conflict. China earlier expressed its ire in terms of strong displeasure.

"The U.S. is using its force to bully the weak," China's official Xinhua news agency said. "The U.S. attack against Iraq...violated Iraq's territorial integrity and sovereignty, thus revealing once again U.S. hegemonism."
"The U.S. attack against Iraq...was designed to meet the needs of its coming presidential election and...help safeguard its strategic interests in the Middle East," the agency said.
U.S. ships and planes fired 44 cruise missiles in less than 24 hours from Tuesday in two waves of attacks on targets in southern Iraq.
Washington said the attacks punished Baghdad for its weekend military drive into a Western-protected safe haven for Kurdish groups in northern Iraq.
Earlier on Thursday, China called on Washington and Baghdad to halt military action in the Gulf, saying Beijing was strongly displeased with the U.S. attacks on Iraq.

"We ask the parties concerned to halt their military actions...and work towards a reasonable and a just settlement of the questions left over from the Gulf crisis," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a regular news briefing in Beijing.

"We feel deep regret and want to express our strong displeasure at the missile attack once again by the United States against Iraq, which has inflicted casualties upon Iraq's civilians and caused property losses," Shen said.
U.S. President Bill Clinton said the attacks had weakened Iraqi President Saddam Hussein and accomplished the immediate U.S. goals.
Pentagon officials denied Iraqi claims on Wednesday that the United States had fired a third volley of missiles at military and civilian facilities in the Baghdad area.
Shen said the attacks only worsened tensions in the Gulf.

"The all too frequent use of force against a sovereign state has not only seriously violated the relevant norms of international law and worsened the situation and tensions in that region concerned, but will also give rise to grave consequences," he said.
"The Chinese government hereby reiterates that the sovereign and territorial integrity of Iraq must be respected," Shen said.
